subject: Token backlog: customer report of intermittent high tail latency
messages:
From: Alex D'Souza <alex@zentext.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 08:14:22 -0700
Subject: Sustained tail latency spikes impacting ZenText production

Hi Connor,

We're seeing intermittent but repeated p95/p99 spikes on the Redwood Hosted API that line up with our highest throughput windows (roughly 09:00-11:00 PT). Baseline p95 for us is ~300ms; during the spikes we're observing p95 > 1.8s and p99 up to ~4s. The spike pattern looks like a backlog builds for ~6-10 minutes, then drops.

We attached a screenshot of our SLO chart and a small sample of request IDs we've seen in the timeframe. Key details:
- Model: rwd-open-std-7b (client pinned)
- Avg tokens per request: 220
- Concurrency: autoscaled in our app but we see request pileups hitting Redwood's endpoint

This is causing degraded user experience. Can you confirm whether this is internal queueing/batching behavior or something in the network path? We can hop on a bridge if helpful — urgent for us.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex D'Souza
Head of Platform — ZenText
alex@zentext.ai

Attachments: p95-trend-screenshot.png

Alex,

Thanks for the signal and the screenshot — I see the periodic buildup. Really sorry for the impact. I'm escalating to our runtime and CS teams now (cc'd). We'll triage immediately and report back with a mitigation plan in the next 60 minutes.

To help our investigation, can you send:
- a few sample request IDs (if not included in the screenshot)
- whether you observed any changes at the same time (model switch, traffic bursts, new prompt templates)

Tentative runbook steps we'll follow: confirm whether batching/queue depth is causing in-flight accumulation, check recent routing/fallback events, and collect a short trace from the servicer. If it looks like config-level batching is responsible we may push a conservative change (smaller max_batch_size) while we root-cause.

I'll coordinate a 30-min call if you're available.

Looping in ops/infra. Alex: thanks for the quick report and the screenshot. I'm attaching a small pack of traces we requested from ZenText (request-trace-logs.zip).

Hannah / Ethan: initial ask: look at batcher queue depth and max_batch_size behavior for the pinned model rwd-open-std-7b during the window 2027-11-03 16:00-18:00 UTC. Also check whether any preemption/fallback routing happened. Prior incidents have shown a pattern where large-request token counts + high concurrency cause KV cache priming and queue accumulation.

I'll keep Alex updated on progress. If we can share an immediate mitigation (config rollback / temporary routing increase), we should do so and then follow with a permanent fix.

On Wed, Nov 3, 2027 at 08:35 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hannah / Ethan: initial ask: look at batcher queue depth and max_batch_size behavior for the pinned model rwd-open-std-7b during the window 2027-11-03 16:00-18:00 UTC. Also check whether any preemption/fallback routing happened.

Quick summary of what I'm seeing from the servicer traces (preliminary):
- Pattern: periodic buildup of in-flight requests at the batcher boundary for the model pool serving rwd-open-std-7b. Queue depth climbs for ~5-9 minutes, p95/p99 increase as a function of batch formation latency.
- Root causes under investigation: large token counts (avg 220) + a recent kernel selection tweak that allowed larger batch aggregation on certain sequence lengths. That tweak increases throughput but raises the chance of long batch waits when request arrival is bursty.
- No evidence of network packet loss or routing failures; fallback events were minimal.

Immediate mitigation (recommended, low risk):
1) Reduce max_batch_size for rwd-open-std-7b from 32 -> 12 (expect smaller batches, lower batch wait times).
2) Temporarily enable shorter batch formation timeout for the affected pool (e.g., 12ms -> 6ms) to reduce tail wait.
3) If feasible, increase pool instances by one small node to absorb spikes (if capacity available).

I'll push the config change to a canary pool and monitor p95/p99 for the next 20 minutes; will report back. Adding mitigation-action-plan.md with the exact commands.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
SRE, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai

Attachments: mitigation-action-plan.md
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:42:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Sustained tail latency spikes impacting ZenText production

Thanks Hannah 12. I pushed the canary with:
- max_batch_size=12
- batch_formation_ms=6
- prefetch_kv=true (helps prime KV cache for common prefixes in ZenText workload)

Preliminary metrics (canary pool vs baseline, 20m):
- p95 reduced from 1.9s -> 420ms
- p99 reduced from ~3.8s -> ~900ms
- throughput drop negligible (~2% on that pool)

I also tested a fast fallback to a slightly smaller quantized variant (rwd-open-7b-q4f) if queue depth exceeds 28 for more than 30s; that fallback is ready as a graduated mitigation but we haven't turned it on in production yet. Plan: leave the canary for 45 more minutes, then roll changes to primary pool if stable.

Ethan Park
Applied ML / Runtime, Redwood Inference
ethan.park@redwood.ai
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 17:32:01 -0700
Subject: Re: Sustained tail latency spikes impacting ZenText production

Alex,

Quick update and apology for the disruption. Our ops team identified batch-formation latency at the pool serving your pinned model as the primary contributor to the p95/p99 regressions. We implemented the following:
- Canaryed config with max_batch_size=12 and batch timeout 6ms (rolled to primary pool after 45m observation)
- Enabled KV prefetch for ZenText traffic pattern
- Standby fallback to quantized variant if queue depth grows again

Outcome observed: p95 for your traffic returned to ~350-450ms and p99 dropped below 1s in the hours after change. We're continuing to monitor and will keep the fallback ready. Full trace pack and the mitigation-action-plan.md are in the shared Drive link below.

Next steps for a durable fix: our runtime team will:
1) Tune the kernel-selection heuristic to avoid the large-batch aggregation for the 200-300 token range when arrival variance is high. (ETA: 2 weeks)
2) Add an adaptive batch-formation policy that responds to short-term arrival rate variance (ETA: 4 weeks)

I know this caused user-visible regressions for ZenText — we take that seriously. If you want, we can schedule a post-mortem and a regular daily check-in for the next 48h.

Thanks for raising this promptly and for sharing traces. Please reopen the thread if you see further regressions.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
